evidence_for: NHL players are allowed to return to the 2026 Olympics, so the US can field a top-level, NHL-powered roster.

US announced a strong 25-player roster (reported Jan 2) with solid goaltending, defense and high-powered forwards; team chemistry was cited as a positive after recent tournament play (4 Nations Face-Off).
Historically the United States is one of the top ice hockey nations and, with NHL talent available, is competitively placed to contend for gold.
evidence_against: Multiple reports characterize Canada as an early favourite with a proven, NHL-powered roster—Canada is traditionally the primary rival and often favored in tournament odds.
Olympic tournaments are short and single-elimination knockout rounds introduce high variance; a single upset or poor goaltending stretch can eliminate any favourite.

Public reporting so far is limited (mostly roster announcements and general previews); detailed bookmaker odds, draw/bracket, injury status, and current form against other top nations (Sweden, Finland, Czechia, Slovakia, etc.) are not available or not definitive in the search results.
open_questions: What are the current bookmaker betting odds (implied probabilities) for USA vs other top teams (Canada, Sweden, Finland) as of latest updates?
Are there any injuries, last-minute roster changes, or disciplinary issues affecting key US players before the tournament?
What is the tournament draw/bracket and potential matchup path for the US (could they face Canada/Sweden/Finland before the final)?
How are the US players performing in the immediate pre-Olympic games and NHL form (goaltending, scoring depth)?
